A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and visual inspection resolves extraction artifacts in tables and equations. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original D4RL MuJoCo experiments, simulated tokamak tracking results, component ablations, prediction-error analyses and training-time measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results on D4RL MuJoCo and simulated tokamak tracking, including ablations and model-prediction analyses.

M1.justification: The Q-value-based penalty already appears in v3 Appendix E.4. Its formulation in v4 Equation (5) adds each ensemble member's predicted immediate reward inside the standard-deviation calculation; v3 Equation (7) uses discounted next-state Q-values alone. Continuous BAMCP, Bayesian belief updates and both SAC and supervised policy updates otherwise retain existing procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same twelve D4RL tasks across HalfCheetah, Hopper and Walker2d, and the same three tokamak tracking tasks. The tokamak dataset, target trajectories and state/action coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v4 Table 3 adds evaluated comparisons with TD3+BC, IQL, SAC-N, EDAC and Decision Transformer, substantially broadening the model-free comparator families. Optimized also enters the enhanced BA-MCTS comparison in Table 2. MOBILE, CBOP and the CBOP reproduction results already appeared in v3.

E3.justification: v4 Table 3 introduces an aggregate over nine tasks excluding random datasets for comparisons with IQL and Decision Transformer. Matched hyperparameter tables, training budgets, ten-episode evaluations and final-ten-epoch averaging otherwise remain unchanged. The reorganized ablation descriptions do not establish new experimental runs.

E4.justification: The belief-adaptation, search, SAC-versus-SL and zero-penalty ablations are retained. One SL comparison entry changes: Walker2d-medium is 82.24 in v3 Table 1 and 82.84 in v4 Table 11, although v4 Table 12 retains 82.24. This is a limited revision to reported ablation evidence; no new ablation design is established.

E5.justification: v4 Table 3 and Appendix F.3 introduce aggregate standard deviations and Cohen's d comparisons, accompanied by statistical-significance assertions absent from v3. Existing three-seed reporting largely continues, without evidence of increased runs. Explicit seed identities and the prediction-error table's explanation of three-repeat uncertainty reporting are omitted.

E6.justification: v4 adds aggregate baseline and effect-size results, while repeating the 80.25 BA-MCTS average already reported in v3 Table 10. CBOP's published result column is replaced by reproduction results previously disclosed in that table's caption, with HalfCheetah-med-expert changing from 97.71 to 97.91. The SL ablation entry also changes as noted above. Tokamak learning curves disappear, but final tracking returns remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 adds Theorem 4.1 and Appendix B's extensive consistency analysis, including policy-regularity and bounded-value-error assumptions, concentration arguments, auxiliary lemmas and backward induction. The stated error bound includes both a simulation-dependent term and discounted leaf approximation error. v3 contains the root-sampling lemma but no corresponding Continuous BAMCP proof.

C1.justification: v4's introduction explicitly adds a theoretical consistency proof to the contribution statement. The central claims about Bayesian uncertainty handling, continuous-space planning, integration with offline RL and benchmark superiority otherwise retain their previous scope.

C2.justification: v4 qualifies learning from exploratory data by requiring adequate coverage and newly explains limited DIII-D access as restricting baseline evaluation. It also interprets large Cohen's d values as statistical significance. Conversely, Appendix F.1 drops v3's explicit HalfCheetah-med-expert exception when discussing likelihood improvement, despite retaining its ratio of 0.7515.

D1.justification: v4 omits v3's explicit codebase URL, feedforward-policy architecture disclosure and details of the imaginary-rollout evaluation using 10,000 starting states. Appendix F.5 clarifies the implementation distinction between headline results and Optimized-based ablations. Most hyperparameters, training budgets, hardware and training-time information remain available.

R1.justification: v4 adds references supporting the new model-free baselines, Cohen's d and pessimism theory. It removes the discussion and citations connecting the work to offline meta-RL and model-based value expansion, including Dorfman, Choshen and Tamar, and Feinberg. The principal positioning relative to BAMCP and offline MBRL remains.

P1.justification: The evaluation narrative is extensively reorganized from six research questions into sections on belief adaptation, benchmarking, ablations and tokamak control. SAC-based BA-MCTS becomes the primary exposition, appendix analyses are regrouped, and related work and the conclusion are shortened. A new LLM-use disclosure accompanies substantial language editing.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive table restructuring and relocation. Prediction errors move into the main text, component comparisons move to the appendix, and a new aggregate comparison table appears. MuZero plots move to the appendix, twelve-panel plots change grid arrangement, and the tokamak learning-curve figure is removed.

improvement.justification: Broader baseline coverage and explicit theoretical assumptions improve assessability, but substantial countervailing issues remain. Appendix B's proof uses polynomial exploration and depth-dependent widening, whereas Appendices C-D retain logarithmic UCT and fixed, capped widening. Table 3 treats large effect sizes as statistical significance without a corresponding test, and reproduction details are lost. Since most headline performance evidence already appeared in v3, these competing benefits and reliability concerns prevent a confident net quality judgment.
